text:
alice: quick follow-up on the activation-state + operator-shim idea from the RFC. i sketched a small flow we could actually implement in the operator without huge db churn. anyone object to adding a QUARANTINED state before VERIFIED?

ben: curious — what’s the main goal for quarantine vs just VERIFIED? is it about retaining blobs while we run heavy checks?

alice: exactly. quarantine = pull + local integrity checks + optional heuristic scans (p2p metadata, signature checks) BEFORE we hand control to the operator to mutate cluster state. keeps fast rollback paths and avoids partial-activation surprises.

carla: looks reasonable. one tradeoff: if quarantine holds blobs long, disk footprint spikes on constrained onprem nodes. do we GC quarantined artifacts?

alice: yes, plan is timeboxed GC (configurable) + admission gating: if disk low, operator will reject new quarantines and fallback to a remote-proxy pull + canary.

frank: how about failure semantics? if verifier fails intermittently, do we retry automatically or require manual operator intervention?

alice: default = 3 retries with exponential backoff, then move to QUARANTINED-REJECTED and emit an observable event. manual remediation only for REJECTED. hoping that automatic retries will avoid noisy manual work.


david: what about the operator shim itself — do we make it part of the operator binary or ship sidecar verifier that operator talks to over local unix socket?

carla: sidecar gives better isolation and lets teams swap verifier implementations without operator restarts. also simplifies RBAC scoping for HSM/KMS calls. downside: more moving parts.

ben: +1 sidecar. we can use a lightweight gRPC auth boundary and keep operator idempotent: operator only sees state transitions returned by verifier.

alice: rough state diagram i posted to the RFC:

```
PULLED -> QUARANTINED -> VERIFIED -> ACTIVATING -> ACTIVE
                   \-> QUARANTINED-REJECTED -> RETIRED
```

alice: operator shim responsibility: token gating, write activation marker atomically, emit events, handle rollback window. verifier sidecar: content validation, signature chains, optional policy checks, heuristics, metrics.

frank: how does this play with partial component activation? many onprem installs do component-level flips. we need per-component quarantine not global.

alice: agreed — quarantine should be scoped to component IDs. operator shim keeps a composite activation plan and only flips components whose verifier reports VERIFIED. remaining components stay in QUARANTINED.

david: observability: we need traces across pull->verify->activate, and a clear audit record for replays. want to add an activation_id and carry that through logs + events.

carla: +1. activation_id also helps correlate disk GC decisions and retention policies.

ben: security note: verifier should expose a minimal API: Verify(bundle_id, component_id) -> {status, reason, signature_chain_hash}. no secrets in the operator. all KMS calls live in sidecar.

alice: ops-bot: rfc link and state machine diagram posted

ops-bot: <https://rwd.internal/rfcs/2026-07-package-activation-shim|RFC-2026-07> added to #architecture-rfcs, assigned reviewers carla, ben, david. :white_check_mark:

frank: rollout plan idea: start with read-only mode (verifier simulates rejects/accepts but operator doesn't switch to ACTIVATING) for one week on a subset of clusters, then enable full flow with a short activation grace window (5m) before final commit.

alice: that matches my thoughts. final open question: how do we handle air-gapped sites that cannot call KMS? proposal: verifier supports offline-escrow mode where operator provides a signed attestation blob and the verifier runs pure local crypto checks and policy heuristics. documentable, but we need an admin UX for injecting operator-signed escrow keys. thoughts?

carla: offline-escrow makes sense. we should gate it behind a per-cluster flag and require a human-ack step in console for first-time escrow key install.

ben: can we add a compact manifest hash into activation_id so we can reference payloads in audit logs cheaply?

alice: yes — activation_id = sha256(manifest_compact||timestamp||cluster_id). short-circuit for in-cluster lookups.

david: ok looks actionable. next steps: update RFC with sidecar API sketch, GC policy, and rollout plan. i'll volunteer to draft the sidecar proto.

alice: thanks — i'll update the RFC and add the activation_id example + offline-escrow UX notes. tagging reviewers @carla @ben @david for final comments. :thumbsup:
